statement: The conference page lists 'CCW/CONF.VII/CRP.1/Rev.3 - Final document - as adopted', linking to a PDF on docs-library.unoda.org; no other document is listed as adopted, and no separately listed decision on the expert group's mandate.
note: Received bytes identical to the 26 November read (LH050-R064). First listed between 21 November 14:14Z and 26 November 14:14Z. The page's label is the issuing body's description.

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: The document records that at its final plenary meeting on 20 November 2026 'the Conference adopted its Final Document, as contained in CCW/CONF.VII/CRP.1/Rev.3, as orally amended, which will be issued as document CCW/CONF.VII/11', and that it 'adopted its Final Declaration, as contained in the Final Document, Part II'.
note: The issuing body's account of an adoption, not a meeting record. Whether the posted Rev.3 incorporates the oral amendments is not stated; CCW/CONF.VII/11 not read (documents.un.org disallowed; LH050-C093). Supersedes C084 only as to whether adoption is recorded in a text labelled adopted: C084's draft past tense stays a draft.

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: The document says the agenda and rules of procedure were not adopted 'as no consensus on this matter was reached'; that the preamble and declaratory part of the Final Declaration were not adopted 'as no consensus was reached'; and that 'The Conference was not in a position to conduct a formal review of the scope and operation of the Convention and the Protocols annexed thereto, but was in a position to adopt section III of the Final Declaration.'
note: Rev.2's para 16 (C082) lacked the clause on section III. Section III of Part II is headed 'Review'; the document's two statements are recorded as written, not reconciled.

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: Decision 1: the Conference 'decides to endorse the set of elements of an instrument, without prejudging its nature, and other possible measures, to address emerging technologies in the area of LAWS, adopted by the Group of Governmental Experts ... in 2026, as contained in document CCW/GGE.1/2026/3'.
note: Fills the '[LAWS]' placeholder of Rev.2 (C083). The elements document CCW/GGE.1/2026/3 was not read; what the endorsed elements say is unknown to this record.

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: Decision 1 continues the expert group and gives it this task: 'the Group is to elaborate, by consensus, an instrument, without prejudging its nature, that specifies international humanitarian law, including principles and requirements, applicable to lethal autonomous weapon systems, and its implementation, and other possible measures'; its report 'will also make a recommendation on the legal nature and specific form of the instrument, including whether the High Contracting Parties should adopt the instrument as a binding protocol'.
note: An adopted mandate to elaborate an instrument whose nature is left open, not a mandate to negotiate a protocol (contrast proposals C054, C086, C088). No passage uses 'negotiate', 'moratorium', 'human control' or 'legally binding' (text search of the whole document, 27 Nov).

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: The group 'shall conduct its work and adopt its report by consensus and shall submit its report to the 2028 Meeting of High Contracting Parties', its Chair will update the 2027 Meeting, and it 'shall meet for 10 days in Geneva each year'.
note: Compare the pre-conference proposal's 15 days a year and 2028 report containing a draft Protocol (C054), and WP.7's 25 days in 2027 and a draft Protocol to the 2027 Meeting (C086). A reporting date, not a deadline for any instrument's adoption.

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: Decision 5 schedules the expert group's 2027 sessions 'on 1-5 March 2027, and 30 August-3 September 2027' and records adoption of its estimated costs (CCW/CONF.VII/7); para 27 records the adoption of those costs 'in accordance with Decision 1'.
note: Fills Rev.2's '[Placeholder LAWS]' in the 2027 activities list. CCW/CONF.VII/7 not read.

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: Elsewhere on autonomous weapons the document 'Welcomes the work of the open-ended Group of Governmental Experts related to emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapon systems' (Article 8), puts an 'Update by the Chair of the Group of Governmental Experts on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems (GGE on LAWS)' as item 8 of the 2027 Meeting's provisional agenda, and acknowledges the support unit's workload 'including in support of the GGE on LAWS'.
passage_ref: PDF p.9 para 80; p.15 Annex III item 8; p.5 para 44
note: The '[LAWS]' bracket after Article 8 and the 2027 agenda placeholder in Rev.2 are gone. Section III (Article 8) is the part para 17 says was adopted.

context: international law and policy (CCW Seventh Review Conference, Geneva, 16 to 20 November 2026)
statement: The section of the final declaration under which the decisions sit opens: 'With the aim of continuing to advance the Convention and its Protocols over the next review cycle, the Conference reached consensus on the following actions' (section I), and section II 'The Conference takes the following decisions'.
passage_ref: PDF p.4 Part II section I heading; p.6 section II heading
note: Para 17 says the preamble and declaratory part were not adopted, while para 26 says the Final Declaration 'as contained in the Final Document, Part II' was adopted; the posted Part II carries sections I to III without a preamble. Recorded as the document states; which parts were adopted is the document's own account.
